generation.hypothesis: For nominal TaVCrW near melting, replacing TOR-TILD’s liquid EAM references with a high-fidelity moment tensor potential (MTP) will improve overlap with the DFT liquid phase-space distribution sufficiently to permit free-energy perturbation (FEP) instead of expensive thermodynamic integration (TI).
generation.material_initial_state: The starting material will be a compositionally disordered, BCC refractory high-entropy alloy of nominal composition TaVCrW, considered in solid and liquid states.
generation.intervention: An MTP will replace the two empirical EAM references for liquid sampling, and MTP-to-DFT FEP will replace the corresponding ab initio-MD-based TI calculations.
generation.conditions: Calculations will use DFT with GGA-PBE and LDA at 0 GPa. SRO will be evaluated over 2000–2400 K, with MTP training and molecular dynamics using a 12x12x12, 3456-atom supercell.
generation.structural_mediator: The mediator will be an MTP with training errors below approximately 1 meV/atom that closely reproduces the multicomponent ab initio phase-space distribution.
generation.mechanism: Reduced variance of MTP–DFT energy differences will allow rapid FEP convergence. Electronic Gibbs energy associated with a DOS gap at the Fermi level and solid-state SRO stabilization of about 2.4 meV/atom will shift melting predictions.
generation.predicted_outcome: The approach should reduce computational cost by about 80%, potentially approaching a 20-fold speedup, while limiting FEP–TI disagreement to below roughly 0.5 meV/atom. Electronic excitations should shift melting by about 48–57 K, SRO by about 25 K, and predicted melting points may remain roughly 160–190 K below extrapolated CALPHAD values.
generation.baseline: The baseline will be TOR-TILD using two EAM potentials and computationally intensive TI based on ab initio molecular dynamics.
generation.boundary: Applicability will cover nominal TaVCrW and the 2000–2400 K near-melting range. Accuracy will depend on MTP training coverage; high-temperature magnetic fluctuations are expected to be negligible. V/Cr departures from usual GGA/LDA binding trends will limit comparison with CALPHAD.
generation.uncertainty: Functional-dependent V/Cr binding may cause substantial uncertainty in absolute melting temperatures.

falsification_experiment.design: Benchmark MTP-FEP against EAM-TI for the VW system using matched DFT settings and include electronic-excitation corrections.
measurements: GGA-PBE and LDA electronic-excitation melting-temperature shifts
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the free-energy discrepancy exceeds approximately 0.5 meV/atom or if FEP fails to converge from small MTP–DFT energy-difference variance.
